title: Acceptance speeches
paragraphs: "Thank you" is a very polite thing to say when you are given something, and this is particularly important when receiving an award at a prestigious ceremony. But if you're one of the lucky winners, "thank you" is just the start of the most important acceptance speech of your life.

Film, TV and music award ceremonies are all about the acceptance speeches – they are an art form in their own right. They are a chance for an actor or performer to publicly thank people who've helped them. In this year's BAFTAs, Letitia Wright even thanked God for her EE Rising Star award in an emotional acceptance speech.

Speeches are also used as a platform to make a political statement or just to raise someone's profile – so it's important to get the words right. And these words have to be delivered in a short amount of time. For example, at this year's Oscars, nominees have only 90 seconds from finding out they've won to finishing their speech. John Bailey, president of the Academy, has told them they should "get up there and keep speeches brief."

When the clock is ticking, it's hard to say everything you want. Weeping can waste time; bumbling costs valuable seconds. Experts in the field say it's important to be personable, heartfelt and to speak like you're talking to a friend. At the 2019 Golden Globes, Olivia Colman was named the best actress for her role as Queen Anne in The Favourite and gave an endearingly excited speech that ended with her holding up her trophy and sending a message to her family: "Ed and the kids - look! Yay!"

You would expect an actor to be eloquent and able to perform on stage in front of an audience. But for others, such as sports people, it can be more awkward. When Japan's Naomi Osaka won this year's Australian Open final, she said "Sorry, public speaking isn't my strong point so I hope I can get through this… I read notes before this but I still forgot what I was meant to say."

Preparation is key. It's important to make notes that remind you to thank people, say some words of wisdom, and win over the audience. But if you've got nothing to say, accept your award graciously then get off stage before the music starts playing again – just remember to say "thank you"!

vocabulary.entry: prestigious /preˈstɪdʒəs/ adj. 有声望的；声誉高的
vocabulary.example: She was invited to speak at a prestigious international conference.
vocabulary.translation: 她受邀在一场声望颇高的国际会议上发言。

vocabulary.entry: acceptance speech /əkˈseptəns spiːtʃ/ 获奖感言
vocabulary.example: The actor's acceptance speech moved everyone in the audience to tears.
vocabulary.translation: 这位演员的获奖感言让全场观众都感动落泪。

vocabulary.entry: in one's own right /ɪn wʌnz əʊn raɪt/ 凭借自身特质；本身
vocabulary.example: The novel is a classic in its own right, regardless of the author's fame.
vocabulary.translation: 抛开作者的名气不谈，这部小说本身就是一部经典作品。

vocabulary.entry: emotional /ɪˈməʊʃənl/ adj. 情感充沛的；饱含深情的
vocabulary.example: She gave an emotional speech about her experience of overcoming illness.
vocabulary.translation: 她发表了一段饱含深情的演讲，讲述自己战胜疾病的经历。

vocabulary.entry: political statement /pəˈlɪtɪkl ˈsteɪtmənt/ 政治声明
vocabulary.example: The singer made a bold political statement during the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手在演唱会上发表了大胆的政治声明。

vocabulary.entry: raise someone's profile /reɪz ˈsʌmwʌnz ˈprəʊfaɪl/ 提升某人的知名度
vocabulary.example: Participating in this reality show helped raise her profile significantly.
vocabulary.translation: 参加这档真人秀极大地提升了她的知名度。

vocabulary.entry: get the words right /ɡet ðə wɜːdz raɪt/ 措辞恰当；用词准确
vocabulary.example: It's crucial to get the words right when writing a formal letter.
vocabulary.translation: 写正式信函时，措辞恰当至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: deliver /dɪˈlɪvə(r)/ v. 发表（演讲、讲话等）
vocabulary.example: The president delivered a speech on national television last night.
vocabulary.translation: 总统昨晚在全国电视台发表了演讲。

vocabulary.entry: nominee /ˌnɒmɪˈniː/ n. 提名者；候选人
vocabulary.example: The list of nominees for the best director award has been announced.
vocabulary.translation: 最佳导演奖的提名名单已经公布。

vocabulary.entry: keep speeches brief /kiːp ˈspiːtʃɪz briːf/ 保持演讲简洁（speeches为复数）
vocabulary.example: The host reminded the winners to keep speeches brief to save time.
vocabulary.translation: 主持人提醒获奖者保持感言简洁，以节省时间。

vocabulary.entry: the clock is ticking /ðə klɒk ɪz ˈtɪkɪŋ/ 时间一分一秒流逝
vocabulary.example: With the deadline approaching, the clock is ticking for the team to finish the project.
vocabulary.translation: 截止日期日益临近，团队完成项目的时间越来越紧迫。

vocabulary.entry: weep /wiːp/ v. 哭泣；流泪
vocabulary.example: She couldn't help but weep when she heard the good news.
vocabulary.translation: 听到这个好消息时，她忍不住哭了出来。

vocabulary.entry: bumble /ˈbʌmbl/ v. 结结巴巴地说；笨嘴拙舌地讲
vocabulary.example: He bumbled through his speech, forgetting most of his prepared lines.
vocabulary.translation: 他结结巴巴地完成了演讲，把大部分准备好的台词都忘了。

vocabulary.entry: personable /ˈpɜːsənəbl/ adj. 亲切的；讨人喜欢的
vocabulary.example: The new teacher is very personable and quickly gained the students' trust.
vocabulary.translation: 这位新老师为人亲切，很快就赢得了学生们的信任。

vocabulary.entry: heartfelt /ˈhɑːtfelt/ adj. 真挚的；由衷的
vocabulary.example: We received a heartfelt thank-you note from the family we helped.
vocabulary.translation: 我们收到了那户受助家庭寄来的一封真挚的感谢信。

vocabulary.entry: endearingly /ɪnˈdɪərɪŋli/ adv. 惹人喜爱地；可爱地
vocabulary.example: The little girl waved endearingly at the camera.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小女孩对着镜头可爱地挥了挥手。

vocabulary.entry: trophy /ˈtrəʊfi/ n. 奖杯；奖品
vocabulary.example: He proudly displayed his championship trophy on the shelf.
vocabulary.translation: 他把冠军奖杯骄傲地陈列在架子上。

vocabulary.entry: eloquent /ˈeləkwənt/ adj. 口才好的；能言善辩的
vocabulary.example: The lawyer is known for his eloquent arguments in court.
vocabulary.translation: 这位律师以其在法庭上的雄辩口才而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: awkward /ˈɔːkwəd/ adj. 尴尬的；不自在的
vocabulary.example: She felt awkward when she realized she had mispronounced the guest's name.
vocabulary.translation: 当意识到自己念错了嘉宾的名字时，她感到十分尴尬。

vocabulary.entry: strong point /strɒŋ pɔɪnt/ 强项；长处
vocabulary.example: Organizational skills are her strong point.
vocabulary.translation: 组织能力是她的强项。

vocabulary.entry: words of wisdom /wɜːdz ɒv ˈwɪzdəm/ 至理名言；智慧箴言（words为复数）
vocabulary.example: The old man shared some words of wisdom with the young generation.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老人给年轻一代分享了一些至理名言。

vocabulary.entry: graciously /ˈɡreɪʃəsli/ adv. 优雅地；有礼貌地
vocabulary.example: She graciously accepted the criticism and promised to improve.
vocabulary.translation: 她优雅地接受了批评，并承诺会加以改进。

sentences.english: "Thank you" is a very polite thing to say when you are given something, and this is particularly important when receiving an award at a prestigious ceremony.
sentences.chinese: 当你收到别人赠予的东西时，说一句“谢谢”是很有礼貌的做法，尤其是在声望颇高的颁奖典礼上领奖时，这句话就显得尤为重要。

sentences.english: But if you're one of the lucky winners, "thank you" is just the start of the most important acceptance speech of your life.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你是幸运的获奖者之一，那么“谢谢”仅仅是你人生中最重要的获奖感言的开场白。

sentences.english: Film, TV and music award ceremonies are all about the acceptance speeches – they are an art form in their own right.
sentences.chinese: 影视和音乐颁奖典礼的核心看点之一就是获奖感言——这些感言本身就是一种艺术形式。

sentences.english: They are a chance for an actor or performer to publicly thank people who've helped them.
sentences.chinese: 对演员或表演者来说，这是一个公开感谢那些曾帮助过自己的人的机会。

sentences.english: In this year's BAFTAs, Letitia Wright even thanked God for her EE Rising Star award in an emotional acceptance speech.
sentences.chinese: 在今年的英国电影学院奖颁奖典礼上，莱蒂蒂娅·赖特在饱含深情的获奖感言中，甚至感谢了上帝，为自己赢得了英国电影学院奖新星奖。

sentences.english: Speeches are also used as a platform to make a political statement or just to raise someone's profile – so it's important to get the words right.
sentences.chinese: 获奖感言也可以作为发表政治声明或提升个人知名度的平台——因此，措辞恰当至关重要。

sentences.english: And these words have to be delivered in a short amount of time.
sentences.chinese: 而且这些话必须在短时间内说完。

sentences.english: For example, at this year's Oscars, nominees have only 90 seconds from finding out they've won to finishing their speech.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在今年的奥斯卡颁奖典礼上，提名者从得知获奖到结束感言，只有90秒的时间。

sentences.english: John Bailey, president of the Academy, has told them they should "get up there and keep speeches brief."
sentences.chinese: 美国电影艺术与科学学院主席约翰·贝利告诉他们，应该“上台后保持感言简洁”。

sentences.english: When the clock is ticking, it's hard to say everything you want.
sentences.chinese: 当时间一分一秒流逝时，很难把所有想说的话都讲出来。

sentences.english: Weeping can waste time; bumbling costs valuable seconds.
sentences.chinese: 哭泣会浪费时间，结结巴巴的表述也会耗费宝贵的时间。

sentences.english: Experts in the field say it's important to be personable, heartfelt and to speak like you're talking to a friend.
sentences.chinese: 该领域的专家表示，感言要亲切自然、真挚诚恳，就像和朋友聊天一样。

sentences.english: At the 2019 Golden Globes, Olivia Colman was named the best actress for her role as Queen Anne in The Favourite and gave an endearingly excited speech that ended with her holding up her trophy and sending a message to her family: "Ed and the kids - look!
sentences.chinese: 在2019年的金球奖颁奖典礼上，奥利维娅·科尔曼凭借《宠儿》中安妮女王一角荣获最佳女主角，她发表了一段可爱又激动的感言，最后举起奖杯对家人喊话：“埃德和孩子们——快看！

sentences.english: Yay!"
sentences.chinese: 太棒啦！”

sentences.english: You would expect an actor to be eloquent and able to perform on stage in front of an audience.
sentences.chinese: 人们通常会认为演员口才出众，能够在舞台上面对观众从容表现。

sentences.english: But for others, such as sports people, it can be more awkward.
sentences.chinese: 但对其他人而言，比如运动员，在这种场合发言可能会更尴尬。

sentences.english: When Japan's Naomi Osaka won this year's Australian Open final, she said "Sorry, public speaking isn't my strong point so I hope I can get through this…
sentences.chinese: 日本选手大坂直美赢得今年澳大利亚网球公开赛冠军后就表示：“抱歉，公开演讲不是我的强项，希望我能顺利说完……

sentences.english: I read notes before this but I still forgot what I was meant to say."
sentences.chinese: 我之前还看了笔记，但还是忘了原本想说的话。”

sentences.english: Preparation is key.
sentences.chinese: 充分准备是关键。

sentences.english: It's important to make notes that remind you to thank people, say some words of wisdom, and win over the audience.
sentences.chinese: 列好提纲很重要，它能提醒你要感谢哪些人、说几句至理名言，以及如何打动观众。

sentences.english: But if you've got nothing to say, accept your award graciously then get off stage before the music starts playing again – just remember to say "thank you"!
sentences.chinese: 但如果你实在没什么可说的，那就优雅地接过奖杯，在背景音乐再次响起前走下舞台——切记要说一句“谢谢”！
